the capital city of Italy

clue.text: Power group's 10-1 bet nearly comes up

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for a bet is dropped
in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the number written as a word
the Roman numeral for one
to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: Odds of ten to one on a bet, as if a government were gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10-1 looks like betting odds, or a cross-reference to other entries, but it is just TEN and I; BAC(K) follows, and the whole string is turned upside down to give CABINET.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the small body of senior ministers who hold executive power in a government.

blocks.note: a roo is a kangaroo, short form

explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle or perch, especially to rest at night.

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant of old striking a large gong, as at the start of a Rank film.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or award, so a big gong is a large medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal, and gong is informal slang for a decoration or award.

blocks.note: rushed means raced
taken as written, with the dropped h

explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

taken as written

clue.text: Thing to cut out centre one and put in spice

the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Crop grown at a location in Africa

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, starting at the end of the first one

explanation.surface: A harvest grown at some place in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Crop looks like the subject of the sentence, a harvest, but it is the trim signal; the definition shares its last word with the source of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is a former province on the east coast of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal.

blocks.note: surface reading: the way things unfold over time

clue.text: Game plan's to play in spasms

explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the planned methods and moves used to win a match or battle.

a laminate is a thin layer or sheet
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.definitionFit: To culminate is to reach a climax or highest point, which is what peaking means as a verb.

clue.text: Basic urge to turn crude about proposal

blocks.note: surface reading: a small patch of shadow

a row is a line of things

explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, and anything that flies can be called a flier.

clue.text: Oddly, I cross out excellent customers

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Pertinent when not cooped up in gunpowder

pent, as in pent-up, means shut in

explanation.surface: Something relevant only when it is not confined within gunpowder.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooped up reads as one phrase, but up is the turning signal: P and ENT come off the ends of PERTINENT, and ERTIN is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, is potassium nitrate, the oxidiser that makes up most of black powder.

blocks.note: taken as written
